brief:
Israeli reserve soldiers expressed frustration over repeated assignments pursuing settlers attempting to cross into Syria, particularly members of the "Ruwad al-Basha'an" movement, Shehab Wire reported. The soldiers characterized their missions as pointless, signaling discontent with the nature and frequency of their deployments along the volatile frontier.

The patrol operations target settlers affiliated with the group designated as terrorist. Reserve soldiers tasked with these enforcement missions have voiced growing dissatisfaction with what they view as cyclical assignments that yield minimal strategic or security benefit. The complaints underscore broader friction within Israeli forces over resource allocation and deployment strategies in the sensitive border zone.
